statement: Fact effective intervals are half-open (effective_from included, effective_to excluded, NA open-ended); effective_to <= effective_from is refused at construction (ledgr_fact_invalid_interval) and again at seal (ledgr_snapshot_fact_interval_invalid).
notes: src A-001; Applies to membership intervals, trading status, lifetime and sessions; corporate actions use point clocks instead.

statement: Each family is built under knowledge = evidenced (supplied knowledge_time kept, missing stays NA) or assume_effective (only missing knowledge_time rows are filled with effective_from; supplied values are kept) and the choice is recorded in hashed family metadata (knowledge, knowledge_assumption = effective) and in every row's provenance JSON.
notes: src A-002; Mixed families are possible: an assume_effective family with some supplied knowledge_time rows keeps them; the plan still labels the whole family assumption_backed.

statement: An evidenced fact row without knowledge_time does not block sealing: it is stored with NA knowledge_time and reported as audit_only (reason knowledge_time_missing) in the validation report.
notes: src A-003; Runtime never-applicable behavior is in ledgr_availability_applicable (R/availability-provider.R:51), reader B. Corporate-action rows follow the same audit_only report (A-024).

statement: Bars carry no separate knowledge time: an observation's ts_utc is its only clock and the schema has no availability or vintage column for bars.
notes: src A-004; Statement of absence. Bar vintage only appears as bar_vintage_id on upstream_vintage_bound corporate-action rows.

statement: A valid bar that is not at a declared open-session close (a closed weekday, an intraday time, or a date outside calendar coverage) is accepted and sealed as an ordinary runtime bar; the only signal is reason observed_row_outside_expectation in the ledgr_facts_validate() report, with no quarantine row.
notes: src A-005; oddity (A-005): ledgr_snapshot_from_df() does not return or print the report when sealing succeeds, so the flag is invisible on the ingest path; Synthesis s4.4 says such rows are excluded from each cutoff's runtime input; whether runs exclude them is a runtime question (handoff to readers of 6 and 8). See A-040 for sweep alignment.

statement: Invalid observations (unknown or empty instrument, invalid or sub-second timestamp, Date label on a non-open date, non-finite OHLC or volume, OHLC bound violation) are quarantine candidates: they fail sealing by default (ledgr_availability_validation_failed) and are excluded into a hashed observation_quarantine family only with invalid_observations = quarantine and declared sessions.
notes: src A-006; Without facts, quarantine is refused up front (ledgr_quarantine_requires_sessions). With facts but no sessions family, can_seal is FALSE with reason quarantine_requires_sessions.

statement: Duplicate valid (instrument_id, ts_utc) observation keys are rejected outright (duplicate_valid_observation_key) and block sealing even under quarantine.
notes: src A-007.

statement: A sub-second bar timestamp is a quarantinable invalid observation when facts are supplied but a hard ingest error when they are not.
notes: src A-008; Dense versus point-in-time ingest difference for the integrator's path matrix.

statement: Ingest requires finite OHLC within high/low bounds but does not require positive prices: zero and negative opens, lows and closes seal on both the facts path and the dense path.
notes: src A-009; oddity (A-009): The Availability Contract (Unpriced members) speaks of a 'positive accepted current close' at runtime; ingest has no positivity rule; Fixture README note 'OHLC must be positive' is not an ingest rule at 289d57c. Runtime treatment of non-positive closes: handoff to readers of 7 and 9; integrator: runtime side (handoff to 7 and 9, read): the valuation state takes any finite close as an observation (R/availability-economics.R:ledgr_availability_valuation_state, is.finite only), so a zero or negative close becomes a mark; fills require a finite positive open (PIT-08-004) and rebalance sizing a positive close (B-058).

statement: Membership intervals and lifetime rows whose opposing states overlap for the same scope are a structural conflict regardless of knowledge_time, so a later-known revision of the same effective interval (member TRUE then FALSE, known_active then known_inactive) is refused (ledgr_fact_structural_conflict) at construction and at seal.
design_source: rfc/rfc_asset_availability_point_in_time_universes_v0_1_9_8_synthesis.md s4.1 (revision facts are not v1; a corrected dataset is a new snapshot)
notes: src A-010; oddity (A-010): Trading status supports source-local supersession and precedence; membership and lifetime have no revision mechanism, and contracts.md does not state the refusal; Scope for membership is (instrument_id, universe_id); for lifetime instrument_id only (source is ignored for lifetime conflicts).

statement: Exact duplicate membership, trading-status and lifetime rows collapse silently to one row; two rows with the same canonical fact_id but different payloads fail with ledgr_fact_identity_conflict.
notes: src A-011; With supplied fact_id the identity is (family, source, fact_id), so a supplied ID reused with changed content conflicts.

statement: Equity corporate-action rows must have unique fact_id before deduplication, so even two exactly identical rows are refused with ledgr_fact_identity_conflict.
notes: src A-012; oddity (A-012): Asymmetric with A-011: other families collapse exact duplicates silently; The later ledgr_fact_deduplicate call on corporate actions can never find a duplicate.

statement: Trading-status rows take status active, halted or quotation_only, an explicit source, and whole-number precedence (default 0); supersession must reference a known fact in the same source and be acyclic; opposing statuses tied within one (instrument, source, precedence) refuse, while cross-source ties at the top precedence seal as runtime_conflict (status_unknown_or_conflicting).
notes: src A-013; Pre-seal conflict classification is knowledge-aware (a row counts from max(effective_from, knowledge_time); a superseder ends its predecessor only once effective and knowable). Runtime resolution: reader B (subsystem 3).

statement: Lifetime rows take assertion known_active, known_inactive or unknown with an optional free-text terminal_event; the label is accepted on any assertion, including known_active, and an empty string is stored as NA.
notes: src A-014; oddity (A-014): A terminal_event label on a known_active or unknown row is accepted without refusal; Labels are matched byte for byte by the terminal policy (reader of subsystem 10); ledgr defines no label vocabulary.

statement: Membership snapshots are grouped into dated sets by (effective_from, knowledge_time, source); complete must agree within a group; complete sets establish omission while partial sets assert members only; an NA instrument_id or character(0) records an empty set header; row form and members list-column cannot be mixed; set rows are open-ended member = TRUE rows.
notes: src A-015; How later set headers supersede earlier ones at a cutoff is resolver behavior (reader B).

statement: Every membership, trading-status and lifetime instrument, and every corporate-action parent and recipient, must be in the snapshot instrument master or the fact is rejected and the snapshot cannot seal; when instruments_df is omitted the master is the set of bar instrument IDs, so a member or spin-off recipient with no bars needs an explicit instrument master.
notes: src A-016; Bars whose instrument is missing from a supplied master are quarantine candidates on the facts path but a hard error on the dense path.

statement: Corporate-action clocks (entitlement, effective, knowledge, payment) are each optional; when supplied they must satisfy entitlement <= effective <= payment; each normalized term needs its validated flag; complete rows have no refusal_reason and incomplete rows need one; snapshot_bound rows carry no upstream IDs and upstream_vintage_bound rows need both.
notes: src A-018; knowledge_time is not ordered against the other clocks.

statement: Corporate-action constructors take no knowledge argument; row provenance always records knowledge = evidenced even when knowledge_time is missing, and such rows report audit_only.
notes: src A-019; oddity (A-019): Provenance says evidenced for a row with no knowledge evidence; Runtime treatment of a corporate action with NA knowledge_time: handoff to the reader of subsystem 10; integrator: runtime consequence is PIT-10-006 (integrator row: such a row never becomes due).

statement: Non-session fact clocks are always read as UTC: a Date becomes UTC midnight and a zone-less character time is UTC; only session open/close strings are interpreted in the venue timezone.
notes: src A-020; oddity (A-020): A Date effective_from means UTC midnight, not the venue civil date (for venues east of UTC that instant falls inside or after the local session); The adapter must supply instants; ledgr does not map fact dates to session boundaries as it does for bar labels (A-022).

statement: Sealing re-validates persisted facts: a header per scope, instrument referential integrity, half-open intervals, whole-second clocks, membership-set consistency, membership and lifetime conflicts, status supersession and source conflicts, corporate-action rows, session completeness and knowledge bounds against the metadata timezone, and the quarantine acknowledgement.
notes: src A-021; Seal does not check that bars fall on session closes or inside calendar coverage (A-005, A-034).

statement: With a declared sessions family, Date or YYYY-MM-DD bar labels map explicitly to that civil date's session close and a label on a closed or undeclared date becomes timestamp_invalid; without sessions the same labels mean midnight UTC; POSIXct bars are taken as given.
notes: src A-022; Label mapping is all-or-nothing per column: it applies only when every value is a Date or date-only string.

statement: ledgr_snapshot_from_df is the point-in-time ingest boundary; ledgr_snapshot_from_csv delegates with the same facts, invalid_observations and price_basis arguments; ledgr_snapshot_from_yahoo accepts no facts and seals dense snapshots only.
notes: src A-023; The roxygen block for ledgr_snapshot_from_csv sits above ledgr_snapshot_format_distinct_ts_utc (R/snapshot_adapters.R:506); NAMESPACE still exports from_csv. Documentation only, not a PIT rule.

statement: ledgr_facts_validate() runs the same validation as ingest without writing; ledgr_snapshot_from_df aborts with the report attached when it cannot seal but discards the report when sealing succeeds.
notes: src A-024; oddity (A-024): Accepted-with-flag outcomes (observed_row_outside_expectation, audit_only, runtime_conflict) are invisible unless the caller runs ledgr_facts_validate() separately; Not mentioned in contracts.md.

statement: price_basis is NULL, split_adjusted or distribution_adjusted; distribution_adjusted bars seal but ledgr_experiment refuses them (ledgr_distribution_adjusted_bars_unsupported); an undeclared basis is accepted for execution, including with corporate-action facts that post cash.
notes: src A-025; oddity (A-025): Only an explicit distribution_adjusted declaration is refused; undeclared bars may already contain distributions; Corporate-action result summaries print 'undeclared' (R/corporate-action-results.R:447).

statement: ledgr_snapshot_from_yahoo declares price_basis = split_adjusted by default from Yahoo's Open/High/Low/Close columns; the caller may override it.
notes: src A-026; Dense only (A-023).

statement: The caller chooses evidenced or assume_effective per family; ledgr records the choice and ledgr_experiment_plan() labels the family assumption_backed (with reason knowledge_assume_effective or generated_schedule) but no run is refused or marked differently for being assumption-backed.
notes: src A-027; Synthesis s4.2 also names summary() and the survivorship article as disclosure surfaces; checking summary() belongs to the reader of subsystem 12; integrator: answers the reader-12 handoff: the probe run's plan labels sessions assumption_backed (knowledge_assume_effective) while summary() prints only valuation and terminal assumption warnings; grep finds assumption_backed only in R/availability-policy.R (ledgr_experiment_plan).

statement: ledgr_facts_sessions_qlcal materializes every civil date from an explicit qlcal calendar object with complete per-date overrides and records generated-schedule metadata; its default knowledge is assume_effective, the opposite of ledgr_facts_sessions (default evidenced); evidenced generation requires knowledge_time and provenance$source.
notes: src A-028; oddity (A-028): The two session constructors have opposite knowledge defaults.

statement: ledgr_sim_pit_inputs builds the session calendar first and derives bars from it, returning raw frames for the five fact constructors (not sealed facts); knowledge is chosen per family (default evidenced) and corporate actions always carry explicit clocks.
notes: src A-029; Teaching adapter. Its membership frame is a single complete set effective at the first close.

statement: Availability-aware execution activates when the snapshot declares any membership, sessions, trading_status or lifetime family, or when the experiment supplies a valuation policy; a corporate-action family alone does not activate it.
notes: src B-001; Experiment-construction overlap with subsystem 2 (reader A); integrator to dedupe.

statement: ledgr_backtest() (the lower-level compatibility wrapper) builds its config without an availability block, so on a snapshot that declares sessions, membership, status and lifetime facts it runs a dense fold: pulses are bar timestamps, every universe ID is a member at every pulse, fills are stamped at the next bar, and no availability diagnostics are written.
notes: src integrator (handoff B: ledgr_backtest path owner); oddity: the Availability Contract says activation follows declared facts with no mode flag, and the Execution Contract says convenience APIs must build canonical config; probe P13 on the full fixture: DONE, availability inactive, 40 pulses, first fill 21:00 UTC (bar time), NNN a member at every pulse; ledgr_run() on the same snapshot is availability-aware (PIT-03-001).

statement: An availability-aware experiment refuses without a declared sessions family (ledgr_availability_sessions_required) and without an explicit schema-2 ledgr_valuation_stale() policy (ledgr_valuation_policy_required); there is no default stale horizon.
notes: src B-002 + A-030 (merged); B-002: Schema-1 valuation policies refuse with a reconstruct message (availability-policy.R:172-180); A-030: Activation itself (which families activate) is subsystem 3, reader B.

statement: ledgr_universe_members(id) must name a membership scope declared by the snapshot (ledgr_membership_universe_not_found); a membership rule on a snapshot without availability families refuses with ledgr_availability_inactive.
notes: src B-003; oddity (B-003): The inactive-snapshot message says the rule needs membership and session facts, but activation is triggered by any one runtime family or a valuation policy; integrator: also covers A-048's clause on ledgr_universe_members() naming a declared scope (A-048 keeps the family-scope keys).

statement: A character-vector universe under active availability is a fixed basket: the provider's members are the declared IDs in declared order at every pulse, whatever the membership facts say; status and lifetime facts still restrict them.
notes: src B-004.

statement: Under a membership rule the physical instrument axis of the fold is every snapshot instrument; members are resolved per pulse from it.
notes: src B-005; Bars, features and positions are held for all snapshot instruments, including never-members such as the fixture's JJJ and KKK2.

statement: A membership, status or lifetime row applies at cutoff t only when max(effective_from, knowledge_time) <= t < effective_to (half-open; missing effective_to is open-ended; missing times never apply).
notes: src B-006.

statement: Membership sets: a header becomes eligible once effective and knowable; eligible headers are ordered by (effective_from, knowledge_time, set_id); the last eligible complete set resets membership and members are the union of that set and every later eligible set.
notes: src B-007; Order is by effective time, not knowledge time: a late-known complete set with an earlier effective_from does not displace an already applicable set with a later effective_from.

statement: Interval membership assertions applicable at t override the set-derived state of their instrument, and among several applicable intervals for one instrument the last in (effective_from, knowledge_time, fact_id) order wins.
notes: src B-008; oddity (B-008): An open-ended interval assertion keeps an instrument a member even after a later complete set omits it (provider and resolver agree); Whether one universe may mix sets and intervals is an ingest question (subsystem 1); integrator: ledgr_facts() refuses two membership families with the same universe_id, so set and interval rows cannot share a universe through the public constructors; B's probe reached this precedence through internal tables only (read).

statement: Runtime membership is two-valued: an instrument with no applicable membership evidence is a nonmember, while ledgr_facts_resolve() reports the same case as member = NA with reason unknown_no_usable_evidence.
notes: src B-009; oddity (B-009): Two membership resolvers exist (prepared runtime closure and ledgr_membership_resolve_at); they differ in how unknown is represented; BBB at the s9 close (announced s5 17:15 ET; effective s10 open): provider nonmember; resolver NA.

statement: For a membership rule the decision axis is the members in C-locale stable-ID order followed by held nonmembers in the same order; for a fixed basket it is the declared order followed by held nonmembers.
notes: src B-010.

statement: Any nonzero position (either sign) on an instrument that is not a current member puts it on the decision axis as a held nonmember, including instruments that were never universe members (for example spin-off recipients).
notes: src B-011; JJJ (never a member) held appears on the axis with status_unknown under the fixture's status family.

statement: Trading status at t: applicable rows superseded by another applicable row are dropped, the highest precedence wins, and a top-precedence tie with different statuses (or all rows superseded) resolves to conflicting.
notes: src B-012.

statement: Supersession is evaluated only among currently applicable rows, so a superseded status row applies again once the superseding row's effective_to passes or while the superseding row is not yet knowable.
notes: src B-013; oddity (B-013): A superseded fact revives after its superseding fact ends; Synthetic: st2 (active; supersedes st1 halted) ends day 6; AAA reads halted again on day 7.

statement: When the trading-status family holds at least one row, every instrument and time without an applicable status row resolves to unknown and is target-restricted (status_unknown); when the family holds no rows or is undeclared, every instrument is active.
detecting_tests: test-availability-provider-witnesses.R:117 (empty family only); none located for partial coverage
notes: src B-014; oddity (B-014): The shared fixture declares status for FFF and EEE only, so every other instrument is restricted at every pulse (run D: 404 status_unknown decisions, 23 fills, all FFF); Owner unclear: ledgr defaults to unknown; whether adapters must supply complete status coverage is not stated. Contract lists status_unknown in the reason table but not this default; integrator: probe P7 (default fixture): status DONE, only FFF filled, 404 status_unknown decision rows; the fixture now has status_coverage = full for trading runs and keeps declared as the frozen default.

statement: Lifetime at t: among applicable rows the latest by (effective_from, knowledge_time, row order) wins with no precedence or supersession; without an applicable row lifetime is unknown with an empty terminal label, which does not restrict.
notes: src B-015.

statement: Restriction mapping: halted to trading_halted, quotation_only to quotation_only, unknown to status_unknown and conflicting to status_unknown_or_conflicting (status family declared only); known_inactive lifetime to lifetime_inactive (lifetime family declared only); the primary reason is the status reason and all reasons are joined with a pipe.
notes: src B-016; oddity (B-016): The token status_unknown_or_conflicting is emitted only for conflicting; plain unknown emits status_unknown.

statement: The execution view resolves status, lifetime and membership for each actionable ID at the next session open, independently of the decision view.
notes: src B-018.

statement: ledgr_facts_resolve() and ledgr_facts_history() cover membership and sessions only; trading status and lifetime have no public point-in-time resolver.
notes: src B-020.

statement: Session resolution at a cutoff takes the civil date in the venue timezone and the first row for that date that is effective and knowable; otherwise it reports missing_coverage or not_yet_knowable.
notes: src B-021.

statement: The provider exposes facts, decision_view, execution_view, history and identity operations, but production code calls only decision_view and execution_view; history and identity are unused.
notes: src B-022; oddity (B-022): The contract names five provider operations; two are dead in production.

statement: Durable runs and readers build the provider from the snapshot connection; sweep, walk-forward and their candidate folds build it from in-memory bars through the same prepared builder.
notes: src B-023; For the path matrix.

statement: A session calendar has exactly one row per civil date from its first to its last date (ledgr_session_coverage_incomplete on a gap, duplicates refused); open rows need open and close times with open < close and closed rows need neither; coverage_start and coverage_end enter hashed metadata.
notes: src A-031.

statement: Session knowledge is bounded: an open session must be knowable by its session_open and a closure before its civil day starts (local midnight); an evidenced row without knowledge_time counts as late; late rows refuse ledgr_session_knowledge_late.
notes: src A-032; oddity (A-032): An unscheduled closure or early close announced during the civil day cannot be recorded as evidenced; only assume_effective expresses it; Sessions cannot be audit_only, unlike other families (A-003).

statement: Local HH:MM:SS session times resolve in the declared IANA timezone to exactly one UTC instant (ambiguous and nonexistent times refuse); POSIXct session times are taken as given without a check that they fall on the row's session_date; each session's effective bounds are local midnight to the next local midnight.
notes: src A-033; oddity (A-033): POSIXct session_open/session_close are not checked to fall on session_date; Only the sessions family carries a timezone; it is recorded in family metadata and re-checked at seal.

statement: One sessions family (venue) per snapshot: ledgr_facts() accepts two venues but validation and ingest refuse with ledgr_session_multiple_venues; the single calendar applies to every instrument.
notes: src A-034; oddity (A-034): Refusal happens at validation, not at bundle construction; Several membership universes may coexist (one family per universe_id).

statement: The sealed range (snapshot start_date and end_date) is the minimum and maximum bar timestamp over all instruments; session-calendar coverage does not enter it.
notes: src A-035; Bars of instruments outside the experiment universe also widen the range.

statement: Availability-aware decision pulses are the sealed open-session closes (early closes included) inside the requested window, sorted, ignoring the session rows' effective and knowledge times; fewer than two refuse ledgr_run_window_too_short; dense pulses are the distinct universe bar timestamps in range.
applies_to_paths: run resume sweep walk_forward promote reconstruct readers
notes: src A-036 + B-019 (merged); oddity (B-019): ledgr_facts_resolve() for sessions honours knowledge_time (not_yet_knowable), the runtime calendar does not, so an ad hoc closure known only late is applied from the start; A-036: Dense versus point-in-time clock difference for the path matrix; B-019: Overlaps subsystem 4 (reader A); integrator to dedupe; integrator: the public session resolver ledgr_facts_resolve() honours session knowledge_time (PIT-03-020), the runtime calendar does not.

statement: Each non-final pulse's execution opportunity is the next in-window open session's session_open; the window's final pulse has none even when the sealed calendar has later sessions, so availability runs reject its actionable targets with final_pulse_no_execution, while dense runs emit no fill and warn LEDGR_LAST_BAR_NO_FILL.
notes: src A-037 + B-069 (merged); A-037: Window truncation matters for walk-forward test windows; consequences for carried state belong to the reader of subsystem 13; B-069: The last pulse is the window's, not the snapshot's: a walk-forward test window's final decision never executes even when a later session exists (handoff to subsystem 13); integrator: walk-forward probe W1: every test window's last decision is dropped (10 final_pulse_no_execution rows per test run) under carry_test_state although the next window's first session exists.

statement: A run's range is [opening date or sealed start, sealed end]; nothing checks that the session calendar covers it: pulses begin at the first declared session and stop at the last declared session inside the range, bars outside calendar coverage are unused, and declared sessions after the last sealed bar never become pulses.
design_source: rfc/rfc_asset_availability_point_in_time_universes_v0_1_9_8_synthesis.md s4.1 (declared coverage must determine every session in the requested run range)
notes: src A-038; oddity (A-038): A calendar shorter than the bars ends the run early (30 of 40 sessions) or starts it late with no warning or refusal; the config end stays the last bar time; C1: calendar to s30, bars to s40, 30 pulses, config end 2021-04-27T20:00:00Z. C3: calendar from s10, 31 pulses.

statement: The run guard requires at least one universe bar inside the range in both modes (LEDGR_SNAPSHOT_COVERAGE_ERROR); per-instrument coverage is checked only in dense mode (ledgr_missing_bars), so an availability run accepts an instrument with no bars in the window (all-NA bars and features); the two-pulse minimum comes from bars in dense mode and from the session calendar in availability mode.
notes: src A-039 + B-045 (merged); A-039: Sweep and window validation take the minimum from the same calendar function (R/walk-forward-folds.R:649); B-045: Dense-versus-PIT difference for Stage 2(d); calendar overlap with subsystem 4.

statement: At runtime each instrument's bars are aligned to the window's pulse closes by exact instant on every path (durable run inline, sweep and window validation through ledgr_sweep_align_availability_bars): a bar not at a pulse is dropped without diagnostic and is invisible to context, features, valuation and execution, and a pulse with no bar becomes an NA row with gap_type MISSING_EXPECTED_SESSION.
notes: src A-040 + B-028 (merged); oddity (B-028): Silent runtime drop; the same alignment is implemented twice (runner inline and sweep helper); A-040: The durable run path reads the bars view instead (R/snapshot-source.R:76); whether it drops off-pulse bars the same way is a handoff to the readers of 6 and 8; B-028: Ingest reports such rows as observed_row_outside_expectation (R/availability-ingest.R:138); handoff to subsystem 1; integrator: answers reader A's open question: probe P11 seals an extra AAA bar (close 999) on a closed ad hoc weekday; validate accepts it, the durable run sees 40 pulses and never the 999 close or the off-session timestamp; ingest side is PIT-01-005.

statement: ledgr_run without a window stores backtest start_ts_utc as the opening date as given, even when it is earlier than the sealed start, while sweep and precompute clamp it to the sealed start; pulses are the same.
notes: src A-041; oddity (A-041): The contract says the scoring start is the snapshot start when the opening is dated earlier; the run config records 2021-02-01T00:00:00Z; Config start_ts_utc enters config_hash. Run/sweep identity comparison belongs to the reader of subsystem 13; integrator: probe P10: with opening date 2021-02-01 the run and the promoted run both store start 2021-02-01T00:00:00Z (promotion goes through ledgr_run); equity and the sweep's final equity equal the undated run; config_hash differs from the undated run.

statement: Window and precompute boundaries are checked against the sealed range by UTC calendar date: a start on the first sealed date before the first bar moves to that bar, an end on the last sealed date after the last bar moves to that bar, boundaries inside are kept as given, and a date outside refuses (ledgr_walk_forward_invalid_fold_window or ledgr_invalid_precompute_range).
notes: src A-042; oddity (A-042): The comparison uses the UTC date of the bar timestamp, not the venue session_date; for a venue whose close falls on the next UTC date these differ (not probed).

statement: A date-only window end resolves to midnight UTC and so excludes that date's session close, including on the last sealed date, where midnight is before the last bar and is kept rather than moved; a date-only start includes that date's session.
notes: src A-043; oddity (A-043): Start and end dates are treated asymmetrically, and a date-only end equal to the last sealed date drops the last session; C5: window s5..s10 dates gave 5 pulses s5..s9; edge window ended 2021-04-27T00:00:00Z.

statement: Feature state, hydration and execution all start at the scoring start: windows refuse a different hydration_start_utc or execution_start_utc (ledgr_unsupported_hydration_start, ledgr_unsupported_execution_start), bars before the scoring start are not loaded, and the first stable_after - 1 sessions of each window have NA features.
notes: src A-044 + B-040 (merged); A-044: Temporary rule until the WS3/WS4 history-start design; B-040: Temporary rule pending the WS3/WS4 history-start design.

statement: ctx$universe is the decision axis (members plus held nonmembers) in availability contexts and the fixed universe in dense contexts; ctx$ts_utc is the decision pulse (the session close in availability runs).
notes: src B-024.

statement: ctx$members is the provider's member list in availability contexts and ctx$universe in dense contexts; ctx$availability_active is TRUE only in availability contexts.
contract_heading: Strategy Contract / Decision Axis And Eligibility
notes: src B-025.

statement: ctx$vec in availability contexts carries member, held, target_restricted, target_restriction_reason, admissible (member and not restricted), priced, mark_age, risk_mark and mark_source over the axis; dense contexts carry constant member, target_restricted, reason and admissible planes and no held, priced or mark planes.
notes: src B-026; oddity (B-026): risk_mark, mark_source and held are exposed but are not in the Context Contract's bound-field list (risk_mark and mark_source appear only in frozen-holding prose).

statement: Availability ctx$bars holds one row per axis ID for the current session, with NA OHLCV and gap_type MISSING_EXPECTED_SESSION where no bar exists, so ctx$close(id) and ctx$vec$close are NA for an observed-missing session.
notes: src B-027.

statement: Feature accessors (ctx$feature, ctx$features, ctx$vec$feature, feature_table, features_wide) are restricted to the decision axis; reading an off-axis instrument fails with ledgr_invalid_pulse_context.
notes: src B-029.

statement: Asset-scoped state: before each callback ctx$state_prev$asset_state keeps only current-axis IDs and gives new or re-entering IDs list(); returned keys off the axis fail ledgr_invalid_strategy_state; a NULL state_update carries the normalized previous state.
notes: src B-031.

statement: ctx$tradable() returns admissible and priced IDs in availability contexts (a permissible stale mark counts as priced) and IDs with a finite positive current close in dense contexts.
notes: src B-032.

statement: ctx$hold() returns the pulse-start quantity for every axis ID (including held nonmembers and restricted holdings) and ctx$flat() returns the default for every axis ID; both are literal targets.
contract_heading: Context Contract; Strategy Contract / Decision Axis And Eligibility
notes: src B-033.

statement: ledgr_pulse_snapshot() always builds a dense context, even on a snapshot with availability facts: every requested instrument is a member and admissible, a bar must exist at ts for every instrument, and features use the dense engine over all history to ts (no strict window, no scoring-start reset).
notes: src B-034; oddity (B-034): Interactive feature values and eligibility can differ from what a run's strategy saw on the same point-in-time snapshot; Path: interactive inspection; integrator: probe P12: on the point-in-time snapshot availability_active is FALSE and BBB is a member and admissible at s5 (it joins at s10); FFF at s14 (halted, no bar) fails ledgr_invalid_args.

statement: An empty decision axis still invokes the strategy; availability folds accept a zero-length target only when it carries a character(0) names attribute (an unnamed numeric(0) fails), and record one empty_public_domain decision row; dense folds refuse an empty universe.
notes: src B-035.

statement: Every indicator in an availability-aware experiment must declare gap_contract = strict_window (ledgr_indicator_gap_unsupported); list and feature-map features are checked at experiment construction, function-mode features only when resolved (config build or strict compute).
notes: src B-036.

statement: The strict feature axis is the run's open-session calendar; each instrument's series has one row per open session with NA rows for missing sessions, and lifetime inactivity or nonmembership removes no session.
notes: src B-037.

statement: A strict window of stable_after sessions yields a value only when every row in it has finite open, high, low and close; otherwise the value is NA, with no carry, imputation or bridging (volume is not checked).
notes: src B-038; oddity (B-038): Completeness checks all four price fields even for indicators that read only close; ingest rejects non-finite OHLC, so in practice only whole missing bars trigger it.

statement: Built-in SMA and returns are recognized by fingerprint and use masked vectorized series; any other strict indicator runs fn on each complete window, and when it also has series_fn the terminal value must agree with fn (ledgr_indicator_gap_parity).
notes: src B-039.

statement: Feature values do not depend on membership or restriction: they are computed for every instrument on the physical axis from all its bars in the window, so a re-entering member's features span its nonmember period.
notes: src B-041.

statement: Valuation marks (stale or frozen) never enter feature computation; features read only aligned observed bars.
notes: src B-042.

statement: Active feature identity wraps each base fingerprint with the gap contract and expected_sessions_cutoff_causal semantics, the feature-engine version adds the strict helpers when active, and dense identities are unchanged.
notes: src B-043; Identity overlap with subsystem 14 (reader A).

statement: The session feature cache key is snapshot hash, instrument, fingerprint, feature-engine version and window start and end, so facts reach cached features only through the snapshot hash.
notes: src B-044.

statement: Among TTR indicators only single-output SMA on close with one positive integer n and requires_bars = stable_after = n is strict-certified; other TTR indicators carry no gap contract and are refused under availability.
notes: src B-046.

statement: Sweep and walk-forward precompute strict series from the same session-aligned bars per window and refuse a payload whose feature start differs from the scoring start.
notes: src B-047; Path detail for subsystem 13 (reader C).

statement: Strategy targets must name exactly the decision axis with finite values (missing, extra, duplicate, unnamed or non-finite fail ledgr_invalid_strategy_result) and are reordered to axis order.
notes: src B-048.

statement: A target-restricted ID (restricted member or restricted held nonmember) may only be held at its current quantity or set to zero; anything else fails ledgr_restricted_target and ends the run.
contract_heading: Availability Contract; Strategy Contract / Decision Axis And Eligibility
notes: src B-049.

statement: An unrestricted held nonmember may be held, zeroed or reduced without changing sign; an increase fails ledgr_nonmember_exposure_increase.
notes: src B-050.

statement: Before risk, a target that is positive and above the current position on an ID without a permissible mark stops the run INCOMPLETE with risk_mark_unavailable at that pulse, before any fill from it; the stop pulse keeps its decision trace and equity row and counts as fully valued.
notes: src B-051 + C-012 (merged); oddity (B-051): A raw target on a member with no bar on the decision session stops the whole run when max_sessions = 0, whereas the helpers skip that member (B-058); oddity (C-012): Unlike valuation stops (C-008), this stop's pulse has an equity row and is the achieved end; B-051: Run B: MMM at s8 (no bar) under max_sessions 0 stopped at 2021-03-10 with affected exposure 0; C-012: Boundary with subsystem 7 (targets); listed here because it reads the mark plane; integrator: owner ledgr (C-012 used unclear only to mark the subsystem 7/9 boundary).

statement: The risk chain runs after availability target validation; ledgr_risk_max_weight() sizes against ctx$equity and ctx$vec$risk_mark (stale or frozen marks) in availability runs and the current close in dense runs.
notes: src B-052.

statement: Post-risk availability targets must be zero or keep the strategy target's sign with no larger magnitude (ledgr_post_risk_inadmissible); dense runs only re-validate names.
notes: src B-053; Dense-versus-PIT difference.

statement: Availability runs refuse a post-risk target below min(current, 0) (ledgr_short_exposure_unsupported): existing shorts may be held or covered but no short may be opened or enlarged; dense runs have no such guard.
notes: src B-054; Dense-versus-PIT difference.

statement: Target-validation, risk and helper errors are run-fatal: the fold transaction rolls back and one error diagnostic records the condition's reason (for example restricted_target) or fold_exception.
notes: src B-055; Run status handling belongs to subsystem 11 (reader C).

statement: Helper eligibility is ctx$vec$admissible; a dense context without the plane treats every ID as eligible and a malformed plane fails ledgr_invalid_strategy_helper.
contract_heading: Strategy Contract / Decision Axis And Eligibility
notes: src B-056.

statement: ledgr_target_rebalance() in availability contexts keeps every ineligible axis ID at its current quantity, reserves the marked exposure of held ineligible IDs once (allocatable capital = max(0, NAV - reserve)), and sizes positive weights as floor(weight x equity_fraction x A / current close).
contract_heading: Availability Contract; Strategy Contract / Decision Axis And Eligibility
notes: src B-057.

statement: In an availability rebalance an eligible positive-weight member without a positive current close is skipped (kept at its current quantity, weight not redistributed), priced targets are scaled when held skipped exposure would exceed allocatable capital, and the skip is recorded as sizing_unavailable; dense rebalance warns and targets zero.
notes: src B-058; Run C: MMM at s8 and s10 recorded sizing_unavailable and stale_mark_pass_through at quantity 347.

statement: Rebalance sizing reads the current-session close while reservations read the risk mark, so a member with a permissible stale mark but no bar today is not sized; a held skipped member without a finite risk mark fails ledgr_target_sizing_unavailable.
notes: src B-059.

statement: ledgr_target_quantity() gives each selected eligible ID the quantity, every other eligible ID zero and every ineligible axis ID its current quantity; selecting an ineligible ID fails ledgr_invalid_strategy_helper.
notes: src B-060.

statement: ledgr_signal_strategy() maps signals for eligible IDs only, holds ineligible IDs at their current quantity and requires a signal for every eligible ID; its default short_qty is -1, so a SHORT on an unheld ID fails the availability short guard.
notes: src B-061; oddity (B-061): The wrapper's default short_qty = -1 yields targets that availability runs refuse (B-054).

statement: Context signals keep raw values for ineligible IDs and carry the admissible plane as their eligible attribute; ledgr_select_top_n() ranks only eligible non-missing scores, and context selections are always FALSE for ineligible IDs.
contract_heading: Strategy Contract / Decision Axis And Eligibility
notes: src B-062.

statement: ledgr_select_top_n() breaks score ties with order(-value, id), which follows the session collation locale; the provider orders IDs with C-locale radix sort.
notes: src B-063; oddity (B-063): Tie selection depends on locale: C selects B1, A4; English_United States selects a3, A4; Documentation says ties break alphabetically by instrument ID.

statement: ledgr_passed_warmup(ctx, values) considers eligible IDs only and returns TRUE when no ID is eligible.
contract_heading: Strategy Contract / Decision Axis And Eligibility
notes: src B-064.

statement: Availability fills execute at the next declared session open at the open of that session's bar, and the fill event is stamped with the session open; dense fills use the next pulse's bar open and that bar's timestamp.
notes: src B-065; Run A fills stamped 14:30 UTC (09:30 ET). Readers derive a recording pulse (R/execution-timing.R:86-257; subsystem 12).

statement: A restriction resolved at the execution open (halt, quotation_only, unknown or conflicting status, known_inactive lifetime) blocks every fill for that ID, including exits to zero; the target is recorded as no_fill with the restriction reasons and discarded.
contract_heading: Availability Contract; Strategy Contract / Decision Axis And Eligibility
notes: src B-066; oddity (B-066): Decision restrictions allow an exit target, but the execution restriction blocks the exit, so a quotation_only or known_inactive holding cannot be sold while the restriction lasts (the contract states this for halts only); Run A: FFF trading_halted at s14 open; KKK, CCC, DDD, OOO lifetime_inactive at their termination opens.

statement: A membership change between the decision close and the execution open does not block the fill; it is recorded as the informational reason membership_changed_before_execution.
notes: src B-067; Run A: NNN (removed s15 open) and EEE (removed s21 open) filled with the reason.

statement: Without a finite positive open on the next session's bar the fill is rejected with execution_bar_missing and the target is not carried as a standing order; the strategy must state it again.
contract_heading: Availability Contract; Strategy Contract / Decision Axis And Eligibility
notes: src B-068; Run A: MMM decisions at s7 and s9 rejected (no bars at s8 and s10).

statement: Availability affordability accepts unblocked sells that reduce longs first and then cash-consuming fills, each group in C-locale stable-ID order, while virtual cash stays at or above -1e-8; rejected or blocked sales fund nothing, and accepted fills are emitted in decision-axis order.
notes: src B-070.

statement: Dense execution applies no affordability check, so dense cash can go negative.
notes: src B-071; Dense-versus-PIT difference for Stage 2(d).

statement: After planning, a mismatch between recorded and virtual final cash stops the run INCOMPLETE (affordability_reconciliation_failed); after accounting, a mismatch raises ledgr_affordability_reconciliation_failed; each successful pulse records an affordability_reconciled row.
notes: src B-072; One reconciliation row per pulse observed (40 per run).

statement: Fill prices are always the observed next-session open after the cost model; stale and frozen marks never price a fill.
notes: src B-073.

statement: Availability-aware execution runs only on the canonical R fold; an explicit compiled spot_fifo request fails with ledgr_compiled_availability_unsupported before execution.
notes: src B-074.

statement: New availability configs record execution_timing_version 2 (availability_open_v2); a stored active config without it reads as availability_close_v1 and unknown evidence as unknown, and neither may resume (ledgr_execution_timing_version_mismatch).
notes: src B-075.

statement: Execution diagnostics record decision time, execution time and ordered reasons (blocking reasons, then execution_bar_missing or insufficient_cash, then informational reasons); the first reason is the reason_code.
notes: src B-076; Observed reason strings such as lifetime_inactive|execution_bar_missing|membership_changed_before_execution.

statement: The valuation state tracks, per instrument, the last finite close observed at a run pulse (an open-session close inside the run window); a missing or non-finite close is no observation.
applies_to_paths: run resume sweep walk_forward promote reconstruct readers
notes: src C-001; Bars that fall on no pulse are dropped before this state sees them (backtest-runner.R:1004-1023); that alignment belongs to subsystem 4; integrator: no positivity check on the observed close (see PIT-01-009).

statement: Mark age is the number of run pulses since the last observed close, so a held mark ages on the declared venue-open-session clock through halts and known inactivity.
applies_to_paths: run resume sweep walk_forward promote readers
notes: src C-002; Probe: FFF halted s14-s15 shows ages 1 and 2, then 0 at s16.

statement: A mark is permissible when its age is at most max_sessions; max_sessions = 0 admits only a current-session close.
applies_to_paths: run resume sweep walk_forward promote readers
notes: src C-003.

statement: Every axis ID gets one mark_source per pulse from the closed set current_close, stale_close, expired_close, missing and frozen_close.
notes: src C-004; expired_close is a reference older than the horizon on an unheld or unfrozen ID; missing means no observation in the run window.

statement: Mark lookback is bounded by the run window: no close before the run's first pulse is visible, so an opening or carried holding whose instrument has no bar on the first pulse has no mark and stops the run at that pulse with valuation_horizon_exhausted, even when a recent pre-window close exists.
notes: src C-005; oddity (C-005): Opening FFF (last bar s13 close 20) dated s14 or s15 under stale(5) stops at its first pulse with mark_source missing; dated s13 it runs DONE; Walk-forward carry_test_state openings take this path (inferred, not probed). Sweep bars are fetched from range$warmup_start, equal to the scoring start since Cut 9; integrator: walk-forward probe W4 confirms the carried case: fold 3's test run opens with CCC carried (last close s18, stale(3)) and stops on its first pulse with terminal_mark_unavailable.

statement: Availability-aware equity (the equity row and ctx$equity) values every held position at its valuation mark (current, permissible stale, or frozen close) at each pulse; dense runs value at the raw pulse close.
contract_heading: Availability Contract; Strategy Contract / Decision Axis And Eligibility
notes: src C-006 + B-030 (merged); B-030: Valuation marks belong to subsystem 9 (reader C).

statement: Within one availability pulse the order is: post due corporate-action cash, resolve the decision view (from pulse-start positions) and marks, post due scheduled dispositions, resolve lifetime terminals (re-resolving the decision view after any disposition), stop or freeze on exhausted marks, write the equity row, then build the strategy context.
notes: src C-007 + B-017 (merged); C-007: Cash posting sees raw closes (fold-engine.R:520) for affected_marked_exposure, not valuation marks; B-017: Corporate-action and terminal ordering belong to subsystem 10 (reader C).

statement: A held ID with no mark at all, or with an aged mark under exhausted = 'refuse', stops the run with valuation_horizon_exhausted before that pulse's equity row, so the last fully valued pulse is the previous one.
notes: src C-008; Probe: stale(0) refuse, FFF missing s14: INCOMPLETE, last valued s13.

statement: Under exhausted = 'freeze' a held ID whose last close is older than max_sessions keeps that close as a frozen mark, is target-restricted with reason valuation_frozen appended, and returns to current_close on its next observed close.
applies_to_paths: run resume sweep walk_forward promote readers
notes: src C-009; Probe: freeze at s14-s15 with trading_halted|valuation_frozen, exit at s16 at 14.

statement: Freeze entry and exit are diagnostics only (valuation_frozen, valuation_freeze_exited); the frozen set for a resumed run is rebuilt at the last committed pulse from ledger holdings, sealed facts and bars, never stored.
notes: src C-010.

statement: A held ID covered by an effective and knowable known_inactive lifetime row is disposed or stopped by the terminal path before the freeze check, so it never freezes.
notes: src C-011.

statement: Each pulse records stale_mark_reduction or stale_mark_pass_through risk diagnostics for held or targeted IDs valued at a permissible stale mark.
notes: src C-013.

statement: Stop evidence records affected exposure as the gross absolute quantity times the last reference close (permissible or not) of the stopped IDs, NA when any reference is missing, with basis last_accepted_close_gross.
notes: src C-014.

statement: Corporate-action subtype accepts any lower-snake-case code at ingest, while only ordinary_cash_dividend posts cash, only cash/stock/mixed_acquisition dispose, and only stock/mixed_acquisition and spin_off raise quantity effects; any other sealed subtype (for example cash_dividend) seals without refusal, has no runtime effect, and the summary reports fidelity none.
applies_to_paths: ingest run resume sweep walk_forward promote readers
notes: src A-017 + C-016 (merged); oddity (A-017): An unrecognized subtype such as cash_dividend seals with no refusal and no runtime effect; oddity (C-016): A held HHH with a sealed cash_dividend row gets no cash; the summary says 'NONE - supplied facts did not affect held instruments'; A-017: Runtime side handed to the reader of subsystem 10. Fixture README records the same observation; C-016: The sealing constructor accepts any lower-snake-case subtype (subsystem 1); integrator: owner: A recorded ledgr, C unclear (who owns the subtype vocabulary); kept unclear.

statement: Every run, sweep candidate and promoted run builds a corporate-action plan from all sealed corporate-action rows of the snapshot under the experiment's policy (research preset by default), in dense and availability runs alike; scheduled dispositions are applied only when availability is active.
notes: src C-015; oddity (C-015): A dense run holding an acquired parent gets cash and quantity checks but never a scheduled disposition (fold-engine.R:539 is inside the availability branch).

statement: Entitlement and effective clocks inside the run's pulse range must equal a pulse exactly or the run refuses with ledgr_corporate_action_clock_mismatch; clocks outside the range resolve to no pulse and the fact never acts.
notes: src C-017; oddity (C-017): A dividend whose entitlement precedes a window but whose posting falls inside it (next_open) never posts in that window; Known input observation (fixture README) confirmed by reading.

statement: A corporate action becomes due at the later of its posting or effective pulse and the first pulse at or after its knowledge_time; a knowledge pulse after the posting pulse is flagged late_arrival.
applies_to_paths: run resume sweep walk_forward promote readers
notes: src C-018.

statement: Dividend cash posts as one CASHFLOW at the entitlement pulse (cash_posting = effective_close) or the pulse after it (next_open), before that pulse's equity and strategy; payment_time is not used.
notes: src C-019; oddity (C-019): The setting is named effective_close but posts at the entitlement clock, not the effective clock; The fixture puts entitlement on the close before the ex-date, so HHH's $1 posts at s14 while the price drop lands at s15; the synthesis reads the entitlement clock as the ex-dividend boundary (handoff).

statement: A corporate-action row with no knowledge_time never becomes due: its knowledge pulse is NA, so cash, disposition and quantity due pulses are NA and the row never posts, disposes or adjusts, while sealing reports it audit_only and the summary reports fidelity none.
applies_to_paths: run resume sweep walk_forward promote readers
notes: src integrator (handoff A-019 to subsystem 10); oddity: a sealed, validated dividend on a held instrument silently does nothing (probe: DONE, FILL only, gross cash 0, fidelity none) while its provenance says knowledge = evidenced (PIT-01-018).

statement: In an uninterrupted run the entitled quantity is bound from positions at the end of the previous pulse before that pulse's fills, so a fill executing at the entitlement session's open is not entitled.
design_source: rfc/rfc_equity_settlement_post_v0_2_0_2_synthesis.md 3.4 (a buyer on the ex-date does not receive one)
notes: src C-020; Probe: buy decided s13 (fill s14 open), entitlement s14 close: no CASHFLOW, final equity 99990.

statement: A resumed run rebuilds entitled quantities for entitlements at or before its start pulse from ledger events stamped strictly before the entitlement time, which includes fills at the entitlement session's open.
notes: src C-021; oddity (C-021): Fresh and resumed runs diverge: the same strategy interrupted after s13 and resumed credits the dividend (final equity 100000 vs 99990 uninterrupted); Not WS22 byte identity; contradicts the resume-agreement statements in the Persistence Contract and LDG-2980 only for this case. Control (fill at s13 open) agrees.

statement: Cash posts only for a nonzero entitled quantity, as quantity times gross_cash_per_parent_unit, at most once per source fact (posted facts are read back from existing events and duplicates fail closed).
notes: src C-022.

statement: A cash refusal (cash_amount or cash_posting = 'refuse') or quantity refusal (unsupported_quantity = 'refuse') on a held entitlement raises an error, so the run ends FAILED rather than INCOMPLETE.
notes: src C-023; oddity (C-023): The strict preset fails the run (ledgr_corporate_action_unsupported, status FAILED) while a terminal 'refuse' stops it INCOMPLETE (C-026).

statement: Quantity effects of stock and mixed acquisitions and spin-offs never change positions under report_only; recipient instruments are never credited and the summary reports fidelity 'unsupported' with omitted-value estimates.
applies_to_paths: run resume sweep walk_forward promote readers
notes: src C-024; Probe: III keeps 10 shares after the s17 spin-off with no JJJ; DDD disposed for 300 cash with 330 successor value not represented.

statement: A due scheduled acquisition row disposes a held parent at its permissible mark (or frozen close) with basis 'evidence', not at the sealed cash terms; only a last_mark default changes the price, a refuse default stops terminal_settlement_unsupported, and no usable mark stops terminal_mark_unavailable.
notes: src C-025; oddity (C-025): gross_cash_per_parent_unit on a cash_acquisition does not price the disposition: CCC disposes at 49.80 (stale mark age 1) against 50.00 terms.

statement: Scheduled dispositions resolve before lifetime terminals within a pulse, and a refused or unpriced scheduled row stops the run before the lifetime path; precedence is per pulse, so a lifetime terminal effective at an earlier pulse disposes first.
notes: src C-026; Probe (held_terminal_position = 'refuse'): CCC stops at s19 terminal_settlement_unsupported, status INCOMPLETE.

statement: A held ID whose decision view shows lifetime known_inactive resolves through held_terminal_position by exact sealed terminal_event label or the default entry; an empty label stops terminal_settlement_unsupported|terminal_label_missing.
notes: src C-027; The known_inactive state itself comes from the provider (subsystem 3).

statement: Terminal prices are: last_permissible = permissible mark; haircut = (1 - h) times the permissible mark; last_mark = last observed close of any age within the window; write_off = 0; a frozen holding under last_permissible or haircut takes frozen_terminal_position instead.
notes: src C-028.

statement: A disposition posts one atomic DISPOSITION event per ID at the pulse close with zero fee, FIFO realization and cash quantity times price; its meta names source, fact, label, choice, basis, policy id and mark provenance, and replay rejects disagreeing rows.
applies_to_paths: run resume sweep walk_forward promote reconstruct readers
notes: src C-029.

statement: A run config without a corporate-action identity resolves every terminal as 'refuse'.
notes: src C-030; Historical configs only; new configs always carry an identity (backtest-config.R:275-277).

statement: Schema-1 corporate-action or valuation policy records stay readable but executing, resuming, rerunning or promoting into them refuses with ledgr_policy_schema_mismatch.
notes: src C-031.

statement: DISPOSITION and CASHFLOW events are not fills: fills, closed trades, n_trades and win_rate ignore terminal outcomes while equity and realized P&L include them.
notes: src C-032; oddity (C-032): A disposed position never appears as a closed trade (probe: two dispositions, closed trades 0).

statement: The corporate-action summary reports fidelity unsupported over modeled over none over not_supplied, lists every scheduled and lifetime disposition with its assumption label, and estimates omitted value from bar closes at the effective time.
notes: src C-033.

statement: The summary's entitled parent quantity is recomputed from ledger events stamped before the entitlement time, the same rule as resume (C-021), not read from the fold's bound quantity.
notes: src C-034; oddity (C-034): Can disagree with the quantity the fold actually entitled when a fill executes at the entitlement session's open (inferred from C-020/C-021).

statement: Assumed terminal outcomes count lifetime dispositions (including exact-label declared ones) and never scheduled evidence dispositions; the warning names each non-evidence outcome and its declaring argument.
notes: src C-035.

statement: An availability run that reaches the end of its fold, normally or by a typed stop, writes one completion row: intended bounds are the first and last calendar pulses, achieved bounds run from the first pulse to the last fully valued pulse, and complete_performance is true only for DONE.
notes: src C-036.

statement: A soft interrupt (option ledgr.interrupt) or pulse limit writes no completion row, keeps decision diagnostics, commits the equity prefix and leaves the run RUNNING.
notes: src C-037.

statement: Finalization writes an availability run's fold equity facts as the exact achieved prefix together with the terminal status, but a run with zero equity facts (a stop on its first pulse) falls through to dense event replay over every calendar pulse.
notes: src C-038; oddity (C-038): A first-pulse stop stores 26-27 equity rows with NA positions_value and equity although achieved end is NA; ledgr_run_open and a rerun of the same run_id then fail with ledgr_run_terminal_evidence_invalid; A walk-forward test run in this state cannot be reopened on rerun (C-073; inferred); integrator: W4: the first-pulse stop of a walk-forward test run stores 3 NA equity rows with achieved_end NA.

statement: Repeating an INCOMPLETE run_id validates the completion row, the exact stored equity prefix and a recorded stop diagnostic, then returns without invoking strategy code.
notes: src C-039.

statement: A RUNNING or FAILED row with a valid completion row is finalized only: its equity prefix is recomputed from ledger holdings and the valuation state, without replaying the fold.
notes: src C-040.

statement: A resume restarts at the pulse after the last stored strategy_state and deletes ledger events stamped at or after the close of the pulse after the restart pulse, and equity, features and state at or after the restart pulse.
notes: src C-041; oddity (C-041): The event cut is on the close clock while version-2 fills are stamped at the next open, so a fill decided at the restart pulse would not be deleted (no committed path writes one; not probed).

statement: Resumed cash, positions and lots are replayed from ledger events stamped at or before the restart pulse close (including fills at that session's open); the corporate-action plan is rebuilt from existing events.
notes: src C-042; See C-021 for the entitlement divergence this produces; integrator: I_paths P4: three interrupts (s15, s19, s23) and resumes reproduce the fresh run's equity and ledger exactly when no fill executes at an entitlement session's open.

statement: Opening positions are posted as opening CASHFLOW events at start_ts_utc on the first attempt, or on a resumed row that has no events yet.
notes: src C-043.

statement: Once a run row exists, an error or interrupt without a written terminal status records FAILED with the message and re-raises; an unexpected fold error rolls back the fold transaction and then records an error diagnostic.
notes: src C-044.

statement: Resume refuses when the config hash, metric context, snapshot or execution timing version differ from the stored run (ledgr_run_hash_mismatch, ledgr_execution_timing_version_mismatch).
notes: src C-045.

statement: Availability reconstruction rebuilds equity on the open-session calendar through the last fully valued pulse, valuing holdings at their last observed close in the run window with no horizon check, and rewrites equity_curve.
notes: src C-046; oddity (C-046): The public reconstruction entry point deletes and rewrites persistent equity_curve rows; Probe (freeze run): rebuilt equity identical to stored over 40 rows; integrator: I_paths P5: on a DONE run the rebuilt equity equals the stored rows and every reader table is unchanged afterwards.

statement: Reconstruction checks the last rebuilt cash against initial cash plus every ledger cash delta, so an INCOMPLETE run with ledger events after its last valued pulse fails with ledgr_invariant_violation.
notes: src C-047; oddity (C-047): A valuation stop one pulse after a buy decision (fill at the stop session's open) cannot be reconstructed: 'Cash identity violated'; LTB-0203's stopped case has no event after its last valued pulse.

statement: An INCOMPLETE run keeps fills committed at the stop session's open (decided at the last valued pulse), so last_executed_ts_utc can be later than the achieved end and the stored equity prefix excludes those fills.
notes: src C-048; oddity (C-048): Probe: last valued s13 close, last executed s14 open; the AAA fill is in the ledger but in no equity row; Readers that replay the ledger after the achieved end (availability positions, walk-forward carry by last equity ts) see or skip it depending on their cutoff.

statement: Reconstruction of an availability run with no fully valued pulse refuses with ledgr_invalid_run.
notes: src C-049.

statement: The diagnostics reader returns the run's stored run_diagnostics rows in diagnostic_seq order; dense runs return the typed zero-row schema.
notes: src C-050.

statement: The availability reader rebuilds, at each diagnostic timestamp, the provider decision view from sealed facts and ledger holdings stamped at or before that time, and recomputes marks from snapshot bars on the run calendar, reapplying the frozen restriction.
notes: src C-051; Probe: FFF rows at s13-s17 match the fold's frozen and current marks.

statement: For dense runs the availability reader reports every universe ID as member, unrestricted, priced current_close, age 0 and status active at every equity timestamp.
notes: src C-052.

statement: ledgr_run_explain joins one recorded decision row with its availability row and the first execution diagnostic sharing its decision time, defaulting to no_action/no_target_change, and fails ledgr_run_explanation_unavailable without a decision trace.
notes: src C-053; completion_status is runs.status; complete_performance falls back to status DONE without a completion row.

statement: Fill rows come only from FILL events; their recording_pulse_ts_utc is the fill time for dense runs and, for availability runs, the close of the execution session found through a unique filled diagnostic whose prior session closed at the decision time, else NA.
notes: src C-054; oddity (C-054): Durable runs derive the recording pulse from sessions and diagnostics; sweeps derive it from the execution-opportunity index (sweep.R:1509-1518).

statement: print and summary follow recorded completion evidence: incomplete performance labels return and drawdown as achieved-prefix values and withholds annualized return, volatility and Sharpe.
notes: src C-055.

statement: ledgr_compute_metrics() reads the stored equity rows and fills without consulting completion evidence, so for an INCOMPLETE run it returns annualized return, volatility and Sharpe over the achieved prefix, which print and summary withhold.
notes: src integrator (completeness walk of exported readers); oddity: two public readers of the same INCOMPLETE run disagree on whether annualized metrics are reported (see the print/summary row); not probed.

statement: The valuation summary classifies a run frozen, stale or current from held decision rows' mark_source, reports frozen-at-end value and a long-only total_return_if_frozen_worthless bound, and drops frozen rows at pulses without an equity row from weights.
notes: src C-056.

statement: print and summary emit one assumption warning before metrics whenever any holding froze or any terminal outcome rested on an assumption, with no materiality threshold.
notes: src C-057.

statement: Completion readers (ledgr_run_completion, run info, run list) project the stored completion row and take affected IDs from stopped diagnostics; without a row every field is typed unknown.
notes: src C-058.

statement: ledgr_run_open opens only DONE and INCOMPLETE runs; an INCOMPLETE run must be availability-aware and pass completion, exact equity prefix and stop-diagnostic validation.
notes: src C-059; oddity (C-059): See C-038: a first-pulse stop fails this validation.

statement: ledgr_run_compare rejects explicit non-DONE runs and excludes them otherwise, disclosing attempted, done, incomplete and failed counts.
notes: src C-060.

statement: A sweep candidate runs the shared fold with an in-memory handler, a portable provider built from the snapshot's facts, and the experiment's corporate-action plan, and reaches the same final equity as the durable run.
notes: src C-061; Probe: one-candidate sweep final equity identical to the run (99958) with dividend, two dispositions and a spin-off; integrator: I_paths P2/P3: sweep candidate final equity equals the run; the promoted run's equity is identical to the run but its config_hash differs (promotion stores the candidate's feature_params, a run with params only stores none).

statement: Availability-aware sweeps refuse compiled spot-FIFO accounting and dense precomputed feature payloads.
notes: src C-062.

statement: A sweep row's status is the fold status (DONE, INCOMPLETE, FAILED) and its completion_json carries the completion record, stopped IDs and the five valuation flags computed from retained in-memory diagnostics.
notes: src C-063; Memory candidates retain only stale/frozen held decisions, terminal dispositions and stopped rows.

statement: Candidate extraction refuses an INCOMPLETE row (ledgr_incomplete_sweep_candidate) and a FAILED row unless allow_failed = TRUE.
notes: src C-064.

statement: Ranking, review, filtering and selection admit only DONE rows; frozen or assumed-terminal DONE rows stay eligible and carry their flags.
notes: src C-065.

statement: Saved sweeps persist completion_json and INCOMPLETE status, and reopened rows derive the same completion columns.
notes: src C-066.

statement: Promotion refuses INCOMPLETE and FAILED candidates, checks only the snapshot hash, replaces cost and risk with the candidate's, and re-executes through ledgr_run with the experiment's own universe rule, valuation policy, corporate-action policy, opening and scoring range.
notes: src C-067; oddity (C-067): Valuation and corporate-action policy and the universe rule are not part of candidate provenance, so an experiment configured differently from the sweep promotes without refusal (not probed).

statement: Promotion context is written only after the committed run succeeds; a context-write failure warns and keeps the run.
notes: src C-068.

statement: Walk-forward training selection admits only DONE candidates with a finite metric; with no such candidate the no_selection policy reuses previous parameters, runs no test window, or fails.
notes: src C-069.

statement: An INCOMPLETE selected test run marks its fold PARTIAL, keeps its achieved evidence, and ends the carry chain with no later opening state.
notes: src C-070.

statement: Under carry_test_state the next fold opens with the previous test run's last stored equity cash, ledger positions at that timestamp and per-unit lot cost basis; short holdings refuse.
notes: src C-071; oddity (C-071): Carried holdings start the next window with no mark history (C-005), so one without a bar on the window's first pulse stops the test run at once (inferred); Freeze state and corporate-action entitlement state are not carried; integrator: W1: fold 2 opens with the fold 1 test run's holdings; W4 shows the inferred first-pulse stop for a carried CCC.

statement: carry_test_state refuses overlapping, reverse-ordered or gapped test windows before any work, measuring gaps on open-session closes for availability experiments and on universe bar timestamps otherwise.
notes: src C-072.

statement: On a walk-forward rerun an existing DONE or INCOMPLETE test run is opened as recorded; any other existing test run resumes through the ordinary run path with the same window, parameters and seed.
notes: src C-073; oddity (C-073): An INCOMPLETE test run that stopped on its first pulse cannot be opened (C-038, C-059), so its rerun would fail (inferred); integrator: W4: the same ledgr_walk_forward() call repeated fails ledgr_run_terminal_evidence_invalid on the first-pulse-stopped test run; W3 shows an interrupted session resumes under the same session_id.

statement: Walk-forward candidate extraction requires a DONE fold with a selected candidate and a test run; PARTIAL folds are not extractable.
notes: src C-074.

statement: Instrument identity is the exact instrument_id string (UTF-8, no trimming or case folding) and is permanent; ledgr has no alias, ticker-history or series-linking input, so ticker reuse, renames and redomiciles must arrive as separate IDs prepared by the adapter.
applies_to_paths: ingest run sweep walk_forward promote reconstruct readers
notes: src A-045; symbol is display metadata: it enters the rule-1 hash (R/snapshots-hash.R:164) and has no runtime use. Fixture not_expressible lists the cases.

statement: fact_id is derived, never trusted raw: a supplied fact_id becomes fact_<sha256(family, source, supplied id)>, otherwise fact_<sha256(family, normalized row content)>.
notes: src A-046; Trading-status supersedes_fact_id references are remapped to derived IDs within the same source.

statement: Membership set identity: a missing set_id is generated as set_<sha256(effective_from, knowledge_time, source)>; each dated group must resolve to one set_id, unique within its universe.
notes: src A-047.

statement: Facts bundles hold one family per (family, scope_id): membership scope is universe_id, status and lifetime scope is instrument, corporate actions equity, sessions venue_id; a second family with the same key is refused (ledgr_duplicate_fact_family).
notes: src A-048; integrator: the ledgr_universe_members() naming clause moved to PIT-03-004; the duplicate-family refusal (R/availability-facts.R:ledgr_facts) means membership snapshots and intervals cannot share one universe_id through the public constructors (read).

statement: Any facts bundle (even corporate actions only) makes the snapshot hash rule 2, covering every fact row, set header and family metadata (knowledge assumption, session timezone and coverage, qlcal provenance), every row's provenance JSON {source, knowledge, payload} with source defaulting to user, and acknowledged quarantine rows; no facts keeps rule 1; snapshot_id is excluded.
applies_to_paths: ingest run sweep walk_forward promote reconstruct readers
notes: src A-049; What enters identity only; hash computation and verification are out of scope (WS5).

statement: config_hash covers data.snapshot_id (a store-local name) but not snapshot_hash: identical bars sealed under two snapshot IDs give equal snapshot hashes and different config hashes; run listings join snapshot_hash from the snapshots table at read time, while walk-forward session_id binds snapshot_hash.
notes: src A-050; oddity (A-050): Run identity binds the store-local snapshot name rather than content, while the Snapshot Contract calls snapshot IDs store-local and walk-forward identity uses the content hash; Each run's snapshot guard recomputes the stored hash before executing (R/run-snapshot.R:55), so content is checked at run time but not recorded in config identity.

statement: An availability-aware config adds an availability block (active, declared_families, universe_rule, valuation_policy, provider_version ledgr_availability_provider_v1, execution_timing_version 2) that enters config_hash; dense configs omit it entirely; fact content enters run identity only through the snapshot reference.
notes: src A-051; Experiment-level headers (family metadata) are kept on the experiment object but are not copied into the config.

statement: A declared price_basis is recorded in config data and changes config_hash; an undeclared basis is omitted.
notes: src A-052.
